title: Oil 101: Antigravity
author: Morgan Downey
description: The updated 2026 edition. Fully expanded with new chapters on the Hormuz Crisis, US LNG exports, and the energy transition. Features programmatically compiled premium SVG charts for offline analysis.

title: NatGas 101
author: Morgan Downey
description: The comprehensive guide to North American natural gas markets. Covers physical infrastructure, pipelines, storage mechanics, LNG export terminals, pricing hubs, and power generation dynamics.

title: The Price of Time
author: Edward Chancellor
description: A comprehensive history of interest rates, explaining how central bank intervention and cheap credit distort asset prices, fuel debt bubbles, and cause financial instability.

title: Antifragile
author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
description: Explores how some systems, businesses, and portfolios benefit from randomness, volatility, and disorder, and offers a blueprint for building antifragile structures.

title: The Ascent of Money
author: Niall Ferguson
description: A financial history of the world, tracing the evolution of money, banking, bond markets, insurance, stock markets, and real estate, showing how finance underpins human progress.

title: Beating the Street
author: Peter Lynch
description: The legendary manager of the Fidelity Magellan Fund shares his stock-picking advice, investment strategies, and stories of market success.

title: Market Wizards
author: Jack D. Schwager
description: Timeless interviews with top traders, revealing the trading rules, risk control strategies, and mental discipline that enabled them to consistently beat the markets.

title: The Intelligent Investor
author: Benjamin Graham
description: The classic text on value investing, teaching the key concepts of 'margin of safety', 'Mr. Market', and defensive vs. enterprising investment portfolios.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
description: Nineteen short stories exploring the strange ways people think about money, demonstrating that doing well with money is more about behavior than intelligence.

title: The Big Short
author: Michael Lewis
description: A narrative of the eccentric investors who predicted the collapse of the US housing bubble, shorted subprime mortgage-backed securities, and won big.

title: The Bond King
author: Mary Childs
description: A biography of Bill Gross, the co-founder of PIMCO, tracing his rise to dominance in the fixed-income market and his eventual dramatic fall.

title: The Case for Gold
author: Ron Paul
description: A critical analysis of monetary history, fiat money inflation, the Federal Reserve system, and the policy arguments for returning to a gold standard.

title: Central Banking 101
author: Joseph Wang
description: A practical, easy-to-understand breakdown of the Federal Reserve, monetary mechanics, repo markets, quantitative easing, and shadow banking.

title: Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits
author: Philip A. Fisher
description: Classic investment guide highlighting qualitative business research, the 'scuttlebutt' method, and the 15 points to look for in a growth stock.

title: Debt
author: David Graeber
description: A historical exploration of debt as a social and moral obligation rather than a simple economic transaction, covering 5,000 years of civilization.

title: The Deficit Myth
author: Stephanie Kelton
description: An introduction to Modern Monetary Theory (MMT), redefining the concepts of government budget deficits, sovereign currency, and public spending.

title: The End of Indexing
author: Niels Joachim Gormsen
description: Examines the long-term trends of passive index investing, active management, and how market structures change when index funds dominate asset flows.

title: The Euro
author: Stiglitz, Joseph E.
description: A Nobel laureate's critique of the structural flaws of the European single currency and how it exacerbated economic crises in southern Europe.

title: Flash Boys
author: Lewis, Michael
description: Investigates the rise of high-frequency trading (HFT) in financial markets, detailing how speed advantages allowed traders to front-run retail investors.

title: Going Infinite
author: Michael Lewis
description: A close-up portrait of Sam Bankman-Fried, tracking the dizzying growth of FTX and Alameda Research and their sudden, spectacular bankruptcy.

title: The Gray Rhino
author: Michele Wucker
description: Introduces a framework for identifying, anticipating, and responding to high-probability, high-impact crises that we choose to ignore until it is too late.

title: Hoodwinked
author: John Perkins
description: An exposé on how corporate greed, debt manipulation, and corrupt economic arrangements systematically exploit developing nations and hollow out the US economy.

title: How to Listen When Markets Speak
author: Lawrence G. McDonald
description: A guide to understanding macroeconomic indicators, debt cycles, credit defaults, and systemic vulnerabilities to successfully manage market risk.

title: How to Make Money in Stocks
author: William J. O'Neil
description: Presents the CAN SLIM methodology for growth stock investing, combining fundamentals like earnings growth with technical analysis and chart patterns.

title: The Intelligent Option Investor
author: Erik Kobayashi-Solomon
description: Applies the concepts of Benjamin Graham's value investing to options trading, showing how to purchase call options as long-term business investments.

title: The Intelligent REIT Investor Guide
author: Thomas, Brad
description: A comprehensive guide to analyzing, valuing, and investing in Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) to build long-term dividend portfolios.

title: Liar's Poker
author: Michael Lewis
description: The classic semi-autobiographical account of Wall Street during the bond market boom of the 1980s, detailing the cutthroat culture at Salomon Brothers.

title: The Little Book That Beats the Market
author: Joel Greenblatt
description: Introduces the Magic Formula: buying good companies (high return on capital) at cheap prices (high earnings yield) to consistently outperform indexes.

title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
author: John C. Bogle
description: The creator of index funds shares his philosophy of low-cost passive index investing as the only reliable way to capture broad stock market returns.

title: Lords of Finance
author: Liaquat Ahamed
description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning history of how the central bankers of the US, Great Britain, France, and Germany shaped the global financial collapse of the Great Depression.

title: Lying for Money
author: Dan Davies
description: A deep dive into financial crime, demonstrating how fraud exploits trust, how different types of scams function, and what they reveal about the economy.

title: Material World
author: Ed Conway
description: A journey through the raw materials that build civilization—sand, salt, iron, copper, oil, and lithium—exploring the supply chains and geology that run our world.

title: The Money Culture
author: Michael Lewis
description: A collection of essays documenting the greed, absurdities, and eccentric personalities of Wall Street and global financial centers in the late 1980s.

title: The Next Millionaire Next Door
author: Ph. J. D. Stanley
description: Updates the classic study of wealth in America, outlining the thrift, lifestyle choices, and wealth-building behaviors of self-made millionaires.

title: The Next Perfect Trade
author: Alex Gurevich
description: A former macro hedge fund manager outlines his framework for identifying high-probability macro trades, focusing on risk-reward asymmetry.

title: One Up on Wall Street
author: Peter Lynch
description: Explains how individual investors can discover multi-bagger stocks before Wall Street professionals do by simply observing everyday consumer trends.

title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
author: Charles T. Munger
description: The collected wit, wisdom, speeches, and lectures of Charlie Munger, highlighting his 'latticework of mental models' approach to investing.

title: Quantitative Momentum
author: Gray, Wesley R.,Vogel, Jack R.
description: A quantitative guide to momentum investing, explaining why buying high-performing assets works and how to build systematic momentum models.

title: Reminiscences of a Stock Operator
author: Edwin Lefèvre
description: The thinly veiled biography of Jesse Livermore, one of the greatest stock and commodity traders of all time, packed with timeless trading wisdom.

title: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
author: Burton G. Malkiel
description: The seminal book advocating for passive investing and explaining the Efficient Market Hypothesis, arguing that cheap index funds outperform active managers.

title: Stock Market Wizards
author: Jack D. Schwager
description: Interviews with top stock traders who achieved astronomical returns during the internet boom, analyzing their methodologies and mindsets.

title: Trading Like a Stock Market Wizard
author: Minervini, Mark
description: A detailed handbook outlining the SEPA (Specific Entry Point Analysis) method for buying explosive growth stocks while keeping risk strictly controlled.

title: The World for Sale
author: Javier Blas and Jack Farchy
description: A gripping history of the commodity traders and firms that buy, sell, and transport the Earth's natural resources, influencing global geopolitics.
